pmsampsize: Sample Size Calculations for Clinical Prediction Models

Source: R/pmsampsize-package.R
pmsampsize-package.Rd

Computes the minimum sample size required to develop or externally validate a clinical prediction model. The package has three families of functions.

Model development (closed-form criteria)

pmsampsize() gives the minimum sample size for developing a model with a continuous, binary or time-to-event (survival) outcome, using the criteria of Riley et al. (2019, 2020). The criteria aim to minimise overfitting and to ensure precise estimation of key parameters in the model. For binary outcomes, the anticipated Cox-Snell R-squared can be approximated from a reported C-statistic (Riley et al. 2021a).

External validation

pmvalsampsize() gives the minimum sample size for the external validation of an existing model with a binary outcome, using the criteria of Riley et al. (2021b) and Archer et al. (2021): precise estimation of the observed/expected ratio, the calibration slope and the C-statistic, and optionally net benefit.

Model development (generalised, simulation-based approach)

The pmgen_*() functions implement the general sample size framework of Riley et al. (2026) for a model with a binary outcome developed with any fitting method, by simulation:

  • pmgen_reference() specifies a reference (data-generating) model, calibrated to a target prevalence and C-statistic, from data or from distributional assumptions;

  • pmgen_target_population() generates the population in which the developed models are evaluated;

  • pmgen_simulate() simulates development datasets at each candidate sample size, fits the model (built in: logistic, ridge, lasso, elastic net, Firth; or a user-supplied function) and evaluates its performance;

  • pmgen_min_n() gives the smallest sample size meeting user-specified criteria, and pmgen_compare() compares two sets of results;

  • summary() and plot() summarise and display the results.

See vignette("pmgen", package = "pmsampsize") for a worked example.

Citation

Please cite the package and the methods papers for the functions used; see citation("pmsampsize").

References

Riley RD, Snell KIE, Ensor J, Burke DL, Harrell FE Jr, Moons KGM, Collins GS. Minimum sample size for developing a multivariable prediction model: Part I - Continuous outcomes. Statistics in Medicine. 2019;38(7):1262-1275. doi:10.1002/sim.7993

Riley RD, Debray TPA, Collins GS, Archer L, Ensor J, van Smeden M, Snell KIE. Minimum sample size for external validation of a clinical prediction model with a binary outcome. Statistics in Medicine. 2021;40(19):4230-4251. doi:10.1002/sim.9025 (2021b)
